voltage_standoff_resumed: ^Voltage: *not looking up from the laptop* Still here.
^Voltage: Nothing you say next will be new.

b: ^And not one of my people saw you come.

voltage_confrontation_start: ^But you're late. This place has no security worth the name, and we've had three days in it.

b: ^Bank B's already gone. One keystroke and A and C follow it, and the grid goes down with them.
^One keystroke and it's now, not eight o'clock. The racks go critical, the hall burns, and the grid drops.

voltage_has_leverage: ^Then we do this the hard way.
voltage_threatens_trigger: ^Look at my hand. Then look at the clock.
voltage_negotiation_attempt: ^This site is one test run. The Architect has six cities on the go.
^Infrastructure attacks, and Social Fabric ready to turn the panic into a riot.
^You stop this one. How many of the others can you be standing in front of?
^We'll stop all of them. Starting with you.
voltage_ideology_explanation: ^Voltage: You want the reasoning. They always want the reasoning.
^Voltage: Two hundred megawatt-hours in a shed on a floodplain, holding up a city that never asked whether it should.
^Voltage: Budget cuts, ageing cells, one fake maintenance firm, and we walked in the front.
^Voltage: We didn't make it fragile. We just stopped pretending it wasn't.
^How many does the hall take with it?
voltage_states_the_number: ^Narrator: He answers without hesitating, and without looking away.
^Voltage: Eleven on site tonight. Nine on the night crew in Hall 2, two in the gatehouse.
^Voltage: On the feed, best case, forty-odd. Oxygen concentrators, the dialysis unit at St Aldate's, home ventilators. That's the number Blackout signed, and I countersigned.
^Voltage: You think I don't know it. I know it to one decimal place.

c-0: ^Voltage: A grid that kills fifty when it stumbles was built wrong. Somebody has to make that legible.
c-1: ^Narrator: For the first time something moves behind his face. His eyes go to the laptop clock.
^Voltage: *flat* I don't need their names to know the number.

voltage_owns_it: ^Voltage: There's no version of this where I blink. You should have worked that out on the way in.
voltage_architect_deflection: ^Voltage: The Architect? You'll never find him.
^Voltage: Not in your databases, not on your cameras, not from your informants. Directives come down, cells carry them out. That's the whole of it.
^Voltage: I run this site. Blackout signs for Critical Mass. Above him it stops being a person you can arrest.
confrontation_choice: ^Narrator: The laptop is open on the plant-room bench with the trigger armed on screen, and the red mushroom head of the hardwired shutdown is on the wall behind him. You cannot reach both.

b: ^Voltage: Static's down. So it's you, me, and one keystroke.
^Voltage: You don't get to have both. I'd decide quickly.

confrontation_choice: ^Step away from the bench. You're under arrest.
^Go for the button and let him run.
choice_fight: ^Narrator: He moves for the bench and you move for him, and the plant room stops being a place where anyone is talking.
choice_arrest: ^Narrator: He looks at your hands, then at the door behind you.
^Voltage: Nobody left to stop you. All right.
^Your thumb's on the bypass module. Blackout signed, you countersigned. Tell that to a court.
^Blackout signed it. You countersigned. Tell that to a court.
arrest_taken: ^Voltage: ...A court. Fine. Let them read the casualty model. I signed it.
^Narrator: He steps back from the bench with his hands open, and lets you take the laptop off it.
choice_button: ^Narrator: You break for the wall. He doesn't try to stop you. He goes the other way, for the dock door.
^Voltage: You save your eleven and your forty. I'll be long gone before anyone counts them.
^Narrator: The dock door bangs open onto the loading bay and the cold, and he's gone into it.

b: ^Voltage: It's done. You were gone long enough, and Bank B went with it.
^Voltage: Still standing? Then let's finish it.

voltage_after_trigger: ^Hands on the bench. You're under arrest.

c-1: ^Voltage: Why not. The number's moving already.
c-2: ^Voltage: Take your time. The number won't.

c-0: ^Voltage: I told you the number. The only true thing anyone said in here tonight.
c-1: ^Narrator: He sits against the bench with his wrists zipped, watching the red button he never reached.

c-0: ^Narrator: The loading bay is empty and cold. A vehicle was here. It isn't now.
c-1: ^Narrator: The red mushroom head is still on the wall behind you, and the racks are still climbing.
